object_description: six-storey tower-like archive body with a two-storey flat body attached to the north
geometry_property: articulated concrete frames with shadow gaps
design_condition: the tall archive body develops along the street with the low body attached to the north, taking over the building lines of the neighbouring garage and sports hall and matching their heights at the low part

positive: The height of the lower part is based on the neighbouring buildings while the higher part makes a visible statement
The building moves away from the central garage and leaves an appropriately small distance to the sports hall
The entry chooses its own, powerful architectural language
The interplay of the solid vertical archive body and the light flat body is a successful answer in this context
They are connected by common design elements
The flat part is organised with precisely articulated concrete frames separated by shadow gaps
These are skilfully filled with window elements and trapezoidal sheet metal cladding
The principle is continued in the lower area of the tower-like body
The closed archive volume is clad with grouted natural stone slabs letting subtle light enter
The two uses are spatially and functionally clearly and harmoniously separated and practically organised
Appropriate functionality can be expected
The reading room faces the street so the archive can be viewed appropriately from outside
The work and ancillary rooms are precisely organised and the divisible storage rooms stacked above
The compact vehicle hall allows a good re-establishment process with sufficient manoeuvring distance
Skylights bring the desired lighting into the vehicle hall
The upper rooms are arranged harmoniously and efficiently around a central courtyard
The supporting structure is very simple and inexpensive with moderate ceiling spans
The vertical facade slot is playfully answered horizontally by the ceiling joist
The sequence of open and closed is translated into the structure as ribbed and flat in an elegant manner
This combines the heterogeneous spatial programme into a comprehensive unit
Where the ceiling structure would contradict the programme it is consequently omitted
A wonderful structural proposal
negative: Fire safety regulations at the small distance to the sports hall must be checked
Urban revitalisation of the entrance street would be desirable
The fundamentally correct developments do not seem to have been worked out rigorously in detail
The interim magazine use would have to be specified in terms of exposure
The quality of stay in the inner courtyard above the vehicle hall must be checked
The ceiling of the parking garage will still need reworking
